outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: Minor mismatch in the agent’s description of what was visible on the page (it mentioned “video content, footer links”) versus screenshots showing profile header/ads/overlays; this doesn’t matter if the ratings were still correctly captured.

Critical issues: (1) The agent did not provide the Blitz rating number at all, and did not provide the Bullet rating number at all—these are the core required deliverables. (2) The agent’s claim that it could not observe the Blitz rating is contradicted by screenshot evidence: Screenshot 1 clearly shows “2860 Blitz” on a Chess.com page featuring Magnus Carlsen. Even if that page is not the exact profile module, it is a Chess.com-displayed Blitz rating value and the agent still failed to record/report it. (3) For Bullet, there is no screenshot evidence that the agent ever located the Bullet rating, and there is no confirmed uncontrollable blocker (no CAPTCHA/login wall/error); it appears the agent simply didn’t reach the relevant section (e.g., Stats tab).

What was completed: The agent did successfully open Magnus Carlsen’s Chess.com member profile while not signed in (multiple screenshots show the “MagnusCarlsen” profile header with Sign Up/Log In visible) and there is no evidence of challenging/messaging.

Outcome assessment: The task’s primary deliverable is the exact Blitz and Bullet ratings. Because the agent did not report either rating, the user does not receive the requested information, so the task is not successfully completed.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to open Magnus Carlsen’s public Chess.com profile (while staying logged out and not interacting with anyone) and report his current Blitz and Bullet ratings exactly as displayed. The user would not be flexible on missing either rating or providing anything other than the exact on-screen values for Blitz and Bullet.
